This marked a substantial shift from the previously fragmented and multi-layered legal framework. items.title: CAT Jammu imposes ₹10,000 cost on Senior Advocate for appearing without uniform
items.summary: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)'s Jammu Bench has imposed costs of ₹10,000 on Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai for appearing without uniform during virtual proceedings and making derogatory remarks "about the Court". A Bench of Judicial Member Diwakar Singh and Administrative Member Ram Mohan Johri directed that the cost be deposited within a period of one week. "He seems to be unapologetic for his appearance without uniform," the bench recorded in the order passed on October 7. According to the order, Ganai initially appeared through audio mode and began making submissions without switching on his video. After repeated requests, he switched on the video, revealing he was not in uniform. "While the matter was under discussion, he made derogatory remarks upon the Court," it noted. Ganai was representing a respondent in a service matter. Senior Advocate Abhinav Sharma assisted by advocate Vishal Sharma appeared for the applicant. Additional Advocate General Rajesh Thappa appeared for the State. Senior Advocate Pawan Kundal with advocate Jagdeep Kour and Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai also appeared for the respondents. items.title: Our forgiving nature must end: Supreme Court on leniency to death row convicts
items.summary: In a stark moment of judicial self-reflection, the Supreme Court on Thursday criticised its habit of showing leniency to murder convicts, particularly those facing the death penalty. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu remarked that the Court's "forgiving nature" has at times backfired and caused problems. Justice Datta opined that the court needs to re-evaluate its traditional restraint when examining whether the death penalty should be awarded in murder cases. "Times have changed. In earlier days murder leading to death (sentence) was on the basis of rarest of rare cases, because murders were rare. Is it the same now? Now murder is not a rare (offence)," Justice Datta observed. The judge recounted a past case where the Supreme Court commuted the death sentence of a convict, only for him to commit another horrific crime after being released on parole. "It is because of our forgiving nature that India is facing these problems. Forgive, forgive, forgive, you have to draw a line somewhere. items.title: Shishtachar squads, beat patrolling, cab driver checks: Supreme Court issues directives for women's safety in Delhi
items.summary: The Supreme Court has issued a series of binding directions to revamp preventive policing, public transport security, and monitoring across the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to ensure the safety of women [ In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR ]. The directions form part of the ongoing suo motu proceedings initiated by the Court after a spate of rape cases were reported recently from Delhi-NCR, including a case where a teenager was raped at a public park. In its order, the Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran emphasised that public safety requires continuous ground visibility rather than post-incident response. The Court observed that unmonitored dark stretches, broken streetlights, and illegal eateries directly facilitate crimes against women. "Public safety... cannot be viewed solely through the prism of a response to a crime after it has occurred. items.title: Refusing to marry live-in partner does not by itself amount to abetment of suicide: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that refusing to marry a live-in partner, followed by the partner’s suicide, does not by itself amount to the offence of abetment of suicide without intentional instigation or knowledge that such refusal would have led to suicide. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the observation while quashing criminal proceedings against six accused, including the woman's partner, his parents, sister and others. The Court observed that the allegations, even if accepted as stated by the complainant, did not establish any act of instigation by the accused to drive the woman to suicide. “People react differently to situations and if a breakup ends up with suicide, it cannot always be termed an abetment to suicide. The refusal to marry was not with an intention to drive the woman to death by suicide nor can knowledge be attributed to the accused that on such refusal, she would commit suicide,” said the Court. Justice PM Raval ruled that one cannot automatically presume that selling textile materials containing artistic depictions of a deity is an act driven by deliberate malice. The benches at Mumbai, Ahmedabad, New Delhi, Indore and Chandigarh together approved resolution plans worth about ₹10,416 crore between July and September 2026. Indore approved six plans worth around ₹1,106.66 crore, while Chandigarh cleared nine plans worth approximately ₹1,079.07 crore.
